active_paradigms.idea: Maximin smooth optimization via log-sum-exp soft-min with scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP)
active_paradigms.description: Replace simulated annealing with gradient-based continuous optimization. Objective: negative log-sum-exp(-areas/temperature) over all 165 triangles — a smooth surrogate for min area. Compute areas analytically with autodiff-free hand-derived gradients or use finite differences via SLSQP. Constraints: barycentric coordinates >= 0 (linear constraints, easy for SLSQP). Anneal temperature down from ~1e-2 to ~1e-6 across restarts from multiple seeds (structured boundary + random). This directly targets the true optimum with far better convergence than random Metropolis moves.
active_paradigms.cautions: 165 triangles × 22 variables; precompute index arrays; use barycentric parametrization so constraints are simple bounds u,v,w>=0, u+v+w=1 (reduce to 22 free vars); fall back to current SA result if SLSQP fails.

active_paradigms.idea: LP-based maximin lower-bound search with scipy.optimize.linprog
active_paradigms.description: At any configuration, each triangle area is a (piecewise) linear function of one point's position when others are fixed. Iteratively solve: maximize t subject to area_i >= t for all triangles, linearizing |cross| by fixing signs (signs change rarely near optimum). Use scipy.optimize.linprog per iteration over all 22 coordinates with sign-fixed linear area constraints and triangle-bound constraints; update signs and repeat. This is essentially a Goldfarb-Idnani / LP-annealing approach that converges to a KKT point of the maximin problem and can escape poor local minima found by SA. Warm-start from the current best configuration and also from symmetric structured seeds (e.g., points on 3-fold symmetric orbits).
active_paradigms.cautions: Handle degenerate sign flips by re-checking signs after each LP solve; project results into triangle; keep SA fallback for robustness.

active_paradigms.idea: Exploit symmetry: search over 3-fold symmetric and layered-boundary configurations
active_paradigms.description: Known good Heilbronn configurations for small n place points on the boundary with symmetric structure. Restrict search to configurations invariant under the triangle's 120° rotation: orbits of size 1 (center) or 3. With 11 points, use e.g. orbits {3,3,3,1} or {3,3,3,2-ish boundary}, reducing dimensionality from 22 to ~8 free parameters (each orbit parameterized by one radial/edge parameter). Run dense multi-start local search (or the existing SA) in this low-dimensional space, plus variants with reflection symmetry. Low dimensionality allows near-exhaustive grid refinement to global optimality within the symmetry class, likely beating the unconstrained SA's local minimum. Also try 'onion' configurations: points on nested similar triangles.
active_paradigms.cautions: Symmetric configs may be suboptimal vs asymmetric ones; test several orbit decompositions; keep tolerance 1e-6 for boundary points; verify all points inside triangle.
